mainTopic: Oaths and guarding responsibility for הקדש, and רבי שמעון's rule about קדשים one must replace
overview: This amud finishes quoting a משנה from מסכת שקלים about agents who lost the שקלים they were carrying and must swear about them. That seems to clash with our rule that no oath is taken about הקדש. שמואל says the agents were paid and swear only to collect their wages. רבה defends this reading against two challenges. רבי יוחנן instead says the משנה follows רבי שמעון, but this answer fails once the Temple collection has been made. So רבי אלעזר says the oath is a rule of the חכמים to protect הקדש. Next, רב יוסף בר חמא raises a ברייתא that seems to make a paid guard of holy items pay. The answer, from רב ששת and רבי יוחנן, is that those workers took on responsibility with a קנין. Finally, a ברייתא gives the source for רבי שמעון's rule about קדשים one must replace, and רבי יצחק בר אבא protests that it looks backwards.

steps.title: End of the quoted משנה about lost שקלים
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה finishes. The agents swear to the treasurers, or to the townspeople, and the townspeople give replacement שקלים. If the originals turn up, both sets become שקלים, but they do not count for next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: They swear to the treasurers. If not, they swear to the townspeople, and the townspeople give other shekels in their place. If the coins were found, or the thieves returned them, both sets are shekels, and they do not count for them toward next year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a משנה in מסכת שקלים about agents who lost the שקלים they were carrying. This quote is being used as a challenge, because it shows an oath being taken about הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה taught that we do not swear oaths about הקדש. Yet this משנה has agents swearing about lost שקלים, which are הקדש money. The question hanging in the air is how the two fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: The treasurers of the בית המקדש
The people of the town who sent the שקלים
They give their שקל (half-shekel) payment
The yearly half-shekel coins given to the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of the quote. The beginning of this משנה (about townspeople who sent their שקלים with agents, and the coins were stolen or lost) came just before this point. Here we only see its ending.

phrases.english: They take an oath to the treasurers;
and if not, they take an oath to the people of the town,
phrases.notes: 'If not' means the money had not yet been officially taken from the Temple collection, so the coins still belong to the town.

phrases.english: and the people of the town give other shekels in their place.
If they were found, or the thieves returned them,
both these and those are shekels,
and they do not count for them toward the following year.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁבָּעִין לַגִּזְבָּרִין, וְאִם לָאו – נִשְׁבָּעִין לִבְנֵי הָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a quotation that began just before this point. It challenges the rule that oaths are not taken about הקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in our משנה that one does not swear about הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in שקלים has agents swearing about lost שקלים, which is הקדש money. That seems to contradict our rule.

steps.title: שמואל: the agents were paid and swear to get their wages
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the agents in that משנה were paid. They swear only so that they can collect their wages, not to avoid paying back the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Here we are dealing with a paid bailee, and they swear in order to collect their wages.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge. The oath in מסכת שקלים is not about the הקדש money itself. It is about the agents' own pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'no oath about הקדש' concerns swearing to get out of paying for הקדש. Here the oath is about something else: the agents prove they did their job properly so they can claim their wages. That kind of oath does not contradict our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone paid to guard or carry an item (a paid שומר)
We are dealing with
Their wages

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the purpose of an oath matters. The same oath can be allowed or not, depending on what it is trying to win.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הָכָא בְּנוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Shmuel said: Here we are dealing with a paid bailee,
and they take an oath in order to collect their wages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הָכָא בְּנוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 1 by redefining the case and the purpose of the oath.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (paid agents) and the purpose of the oath (wages, not liability)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The agents swear to avoid paying back lost הקדש money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The agents are paid, and they swear only to collect their wages.

steps.title: If it is about wages, why swear to the treasurers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל. If the oath is to collect wages, it should be made to the townspeople who pay those wages, not to the treasurers.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'they swear to the treasurers'? It should have said 'to the people of the town'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל using the wording of the משנה. The person you swear to should be the one you are claiming money from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל's reading, the agents want their pay from the townspeople who hired them. Yet the משנה says they swear to the treasurers, who owe them nothing. That wording does not fit שמואל's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge to what was just said)
It should have said

phrases.english: If so, is it right to say they take an oath to the treasurers?
It should have said: to the people of the town!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer from step 2 using the wording of the quoted משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the oath is about collecting wages
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wages come from the townspeople, so the oath should be made to them. The משנה says the treasurers.

steps.title: רבה: they swear to the townspeople while the treasurers are present
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the oath is made to the townspeople but in front of the treasurers. He gives two reasons for having the treasurers there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: They swear to the people of the town in the presence of the treasurers, so that the treasurers will not suspect them. Or another reason: so that the treasurers will not call them 'negligent'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends שמואל. The oath really is to the townspeople, and the treasurers are only there to witness it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's words 'to the treasurers' only mean 'in front of the treasurers.' Reason one: the treasurers should not suspect the townspeople of never sending their שקלים. Reason two: the treasurers should not label the agents as careless.

keyTerms.meaning: In the presence of
They will suspect them
Or another explanation
Negligent, careless people

phrases.english: Rabba said: They take an oath to the people of the town
in the presence of the treasurers,
so that they will not suspect them,
phrases.notes: He means the treasurers won't suspect that the townspeople never gave their שקלים at all.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי נָמֵי, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לִקְרוֹ לְהוּ ״פּוֹשְׁעִים״.
phrases.english: or alternatively, so that they will not call them 'negligent.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: נִשְׁבָּעִין לִבְנֵי הָעִיר בְּמַעֲמַד גִּזְבָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 3 and keeps שמואל's approach in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording: 'to the treasurers' means 'in front of the treasurers'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath is made to the treasurers, which doesn't fit a wage claim.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath is made to the townspeople, with the treasurers present for one of two reasons.

steps.title: A paid שומר is responsible for theft and loss, so shouldn't they lose their wages?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל again. A paid שומר is responsible for theft and loss. Even if he does not pay for הקדש, he should at least lose his pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'they were stolen or lost,' and a paid bailee is liable for theft and loss! Here too, even if they don't actually pay, they should at least lose their wages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's idea that the agents swear to collect wages. If they were paid guardians and the money was stolen or lost, they failed at the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר שכר normally has to pay when the item is stolen or lost. With הקדש he may not have to pay, but he still should not be paid for a job he failed at. So what could the oath gain them?

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (the משנה says)
Theft and loss
Granted, even if
Their wages
Let them lose

phrases.english: But it teaches 'they were stolen or lost,'

phrases.aramaic: וְשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר בִּגְנֵיבָה וַאֲבֵידָה חַיּוֹבֵי מִיחַיַּיב!
phrases.english: and a paid bailee is liable for theft and loss!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא נָמֵי, נְהִי דְּשַׁלּוֹמֵי לָא מְשַׁלְּמִי,
phrases.english: And here too, granted they do not pay,
let them at least lose their wages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to שמואל's answer (step 2), this time from the laws of a paid שומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the paid agents swear to collect their wages
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A paid שומר is responsible for theft and loss. So the agents should forfeit their wages, and an oath should not help them.

steps.title: רבה: armed robbers and a sunken ship
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that 'stolen' means taken by armed robbers and 'lost' means the ship sank. Both are אונס, which even a paid שומר is not responsible for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: 'Stolen' means by armed robbers. 'Lost' means his ship sank at sea.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers by defining the case narrowly. The theft and loss in that משנה were things nobody could have stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A paid שומר is responsible for ordinary theft and loss, but not for אונס, events beyond his control. Armed robbers and a shipwreck are אונס, so the agents did their job properly. They can swear to that and still collect their wages.

keyTerms.meaning: Armed robbers
His ship sank
An unavoidable accident, beyond one's control

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the משנה in שקלים fits our rule against oaths about הקדש. The agents were paid, and they swear to collect their wages. They swear to the townspeople in front of the treasurers, and the 'theft' and 'loss' were אונס (armed robbers, a shipwreck), so they keep their pay.

phrases.english: Rabba said: 'They were stolen' means by armed robbers;
'they were lost' means his ship sank at sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by limiting the case to אונס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: theft and loss here were אונס
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ordinary theft and loss, for which a paid שומר is responsible and would lose his wages.
steps.terutzMaskana: Armed robbery and shipwreck are אונס, so the paid agents are not at fault and can collect their wages.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer to why the agents swear. The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who says one swears about holy items that a person is responsible to replace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whose opinion is this משנה? It is רבי שמעון's. He says that holy items a person must replace if lost are subject to the laws of אונאה, and people swear about them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן offers a new answer to the original question of why there is an oath about הקדש money in this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there is no oath about הקדש. רבי שמעון holds that if a person is responsible to replace the holy item, it is treated like his own property, so an oath applies. The townspeople must replace lost שקלים, so the oath makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
Holy or consecrated items
Responsibility to replace something if it is lost
Overcharging or underpaying in a sale

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: Whose opinion is this?
It is Rabbi Shimon,
who says: Holy items that one is responsible to replace
are subject to the laws of overcharging,
and one takes an oath about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer that replaces שמואל's paid-agent approach from Steps 2-6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There should never be an oath about הקדש money.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, holy items that one must replace do carry an oath.

steps.title: After the Temple collection, no one is responsible anymore
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's answer only works before the Temple chamber collection. After the collection, the townspeople are no longer responsible for the coins, so רבי שמעון's reason disappears.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works if the coins were lost before the Temple collection was made. Once the collection is made, they are holy items no one has to replace. A ברייתא teaches that the collection is made on behalf of coins that were lost, coins already collected, and coins that will be collected later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. His answer cannot explain the case in the משנה where the coins were lost after the Temple collection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The collection from the Temple chamber counts even for coins that never arrived. So once it happens, the townspeople have already fulfilled their duty and do not have to replace the lost coins. Without that responsibility, רבי שמעון would not require an oath, yet the משנה still requires one.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (only in one case)
The coins were taken out of the Temple chamber for the communal offerings
They take out the collection

phrases.english: This works well before the collection was taken.
phrases.notes: This means the taking of coins out of the Temple's chamber to buy the communal offerings.

phrases.english: But once the collection was taken,
they are holy items that one is not responsible to replace,
as it is taught: One takes the collection for the lost coins,
and for the coins already gathered,
and for those that will be gathered in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's answer from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the collection, the townspeople are no longer responsible for the coins. רבי שמעון's reason for the oath does not apply, yet the משנה still has an oath.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: The oath is a rabbinic enactment
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the agents' oath is a rule made by the חכמים. Its purpose is to stop people from being careless with הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר said: This oath is an enactment of the חכמים, made so that people will not treat holy property lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: After the challenge to רבי יוחנן, the גמרא drops his answer and gives a new explanation. The oath is not from the Torah at all. The חכמים created it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law there may be no oath on הקדש. The חכמים still required one, so agents would guard holy money carefully. This answer works both before and after the Temple collection.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier answer)
A rule enacted by the חכמים
Treating lightly or carelessly
Property belonging to the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: The agents' oath about lost שקלים is a rabbinic enactment that protects הקדש. It does not depend on who is responsible to replace the coins.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar said:
This oath is an enactment of the Sages,
so that people will not be
careless with holy property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁבוּעָה זוֹ תַּקָּנַת חֲכָמִים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי יוחנן's answer after the challenge in Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath must come from Torah law, so it needs a Torah reason such as responsibility to replace the coins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath is a rabbinic enactment to protect הקדש, so it applies in every case.

steps.title: Contradiction: Does a paid guard of holy items pay?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a paid שומר does not pay. רב יוסף בר חמא points to a ברייתא about workers hired to guard holy items, which suggests they are responsible on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a paid שומר does not pay. רב יוסף בר חמא asked רבה: We learned that a paid שומר does not pay. But a ברייתא says: If someone hires a worker to guard the red heifer, the child, or the seeds, he does not pay him for שבת. So he is not responsible for losses on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins with a quote from the משנה. רב יוסף בר חמא is setting up a contradiction, and its full point is spelled out in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties responsibility to pay: a day-worker gets no pay for שבת, so he is not responsible for שבת. The other side of that rule, spelled out in the next step, is that a worker who is paid for שבת is responsible, even though the items he guards are holy. That seems to clash with the משנה, which says a paid שומר of הקדש does not pay.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid guard (שומר שכר)
He pointed out a contradiction to him
And they contrasted it with another source
Here, the red heifer (פרה אדומה)
Seeds

steps.confusionAlert: This step is only the first half of the ברייתא. The clash with the משנה becomes clear in the next step, where a worker paid for שבת is called responsible, and the גמרא asks whether that means he must pay.

phrases.english: A paid guard does not pay.

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא לְרַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Chama raised a contradiction to Rabba:
We learned: A paid guard does not pay,
and contrast it: One who hires a worker
to guard the heifer,
phrases.notes: The red heifer, which must be kept from becoming unfit.

phrases.english: to guard the child,
to guard the seeds,
does not give him wages for Shabbat,
therefore he is not responsible for Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא לְרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section on the משנה's words about a paid שומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a paid שומר does not pay for lost הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies that a paid worker guarding holy items is responsible on the days he is paid. That contradicts the משנה's ruling.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא seems to make the guard pay
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a worker hired by the week or longer gets paid for שבת, so he is responsible for שבת. The גמרא asks whether this means he must pay for the loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was hired for a week, a month, a year, or seven years, he is paid for שבת too, so he is responsible for שבת. Doesn't 'responsible' mean he has to pay for what was lost?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from step 10 and draws the conclusion that troubles our משנה. A worker paid for Shabbat seems to have to pay for holy items lost on Shabbat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The workers in this ברייתא guard items that include holy items. If a worker paid by the week must pay for losses, then a paid guard is responsible for הקדש. That clashes with our משנה, which says a paid שומר of holy items does not pay.

keyTerms.meaning: A worker hired by the week
A worker hired for a seven-year period
Responsibility for a loss
'Isn't it that...?', a phrase used to push a reading

phrases.english: If he was hired for a week,
phrases.notes: Here שַׁבָּת means a whole week, not only the day of Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר חֹדֶשׁ, שְׂכִיר שָׁנָה, שְׂכִיר שָׁבוּעַ –
phrases.english: hired for a month, hired for a year, hired for seven years –
phrases.notes: שָׁבוּעַ here means a span of seven years.

phrases.english: they give him wages for Shabbat,
therefore responsibility for Shabbat is upon him.
What, is it not that he must pay?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 10 and states the challenge it creates.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a paid שומר of הקדש does not pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a weekly worker guarding holy items is 'responsible' and that means paying, then a paid guard does pay for הקדש.

steps.title: Responsibility means losing his wages
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that 'responsibility' only means the worker loses his pay for that day. It does not mean he pays for the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means he loses his wages.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on the reading from step 11. He says the worker is not paying for the lost item; he just doesn't get paid because he didn't guard properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the משנה safe. If 'responsibility' only means losing wages, the worker never pays for the holy item, so a paid שומר of הקדש is still exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: To lose his wages
'No', the start of a pushback
Wages, pay

phrases.english: No, it means to lose his wages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by reading 'responsibility' differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a key word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Responsibility means paying for the lost item.

steps.title: That reading fails in the first half of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר חמא points out that the first half says the day-worker is NOT responsible for שבת. That cannot mean he doesn't lose שבת wages, because he never gets שבת wages. רבה is silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the first part says 'he is not responsible for שבת.' Does that also mean about losing wages? Does he even get wages for שבת? It says they don't pay him for שבת! רבה was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף בר חמא attacks רבה's answer. The answer makes the first half of the ברייתא meaningless, and רבה has no reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half is about a worker who gets no Shabbat pay. Saying he 'isn't responsible' can't mean he keeps his Shabbat wages, since he has none. So 'responsibility' in this ברייתא must mean paying for the item, and the problem from step 11 is back.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a ברייתא or משנה
'Is it also so?', applying the same reading elsewhere
He was silent, had no answer

steps.confusionAlert: Both halves of the ברייתא use the same word אַחְרָיוּת. It has to mean the same thing in both halves, which is why רבה's answer fails.

phrases.english: If so, the first clause, which teaches:
'responsibility for Shabbat is not upon him' –
phrases.notes: This is the day-worker from the first half of the ברייתא, quoted in step 10.

phrases.english: is this also about losing his wages?
But does he have wages for Shabbat?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָתָנֵי: ״אֵין נוֹתְנִין לוֹ שְׂכַר שַׁבָּת״!
phrases.english: But it teaches: 'they do not give him wages for Shabbat'!
He was silent.
phrases.notes: This is רבה, who gave the answer in step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reading that 'responsibility' means losing wages
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word in the first half cannot mean losing wages, since that worker gets no Shabbat wages at all.

steps.title: רבה asks if there is a known answer
steps.stepSummary: After being stuck, רבה asks רב יוסף בר חמא if he heard an answer to this problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did you hear anything about this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה admits he is stuck and asks the challenger for a solution. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is still open: the ברייתא makes a paid guard pay for holy items, but the משנה says he doesn't. רבה is asking for a teaching from earlier rabbis that solves it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Did you hear anything?', asking for a received teaching
About this

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידֵּי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בְּהָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Have you heard anything about this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After failing to answer in step 13, רבה asks for help.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is a known explanation for why the weekly worker pays.

steps.title: The workers took on responsibility with a קנין
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר חמא answers in the name of רב ששת, and רבי יוחנן says the same: the second half is about workers who made a קנין to accept responsibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב ששת said, it is where they made a קנין with him. And רבי יוחנן also said, it is where they made a קנין with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The real answer: the weekly workers pay only because they formally promised to, backed up with a קנין. This settles the conflict with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a paid שומר of holy items is exempt, just as the משנה says. Here the workers took on extra liability by their own agreement, sealed with a קנין, so they must pay. This is a special added obligation, not a change in the basic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they made a קנין with him, a formal act binding them to their promise
A formal act that makes a deal or promise binding
And likewise, another rabbi saying the same thing

steps.whatToRemember: A paid שומר is not responsible for הקדש. The ברייתא that makes the weekly worker pay is about a case where he formally took on that responsibility with a קנין.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an exemption written in the law can still be overridden by a person's own binding commitment.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what רב ששת said:
It is where they made a קנין with him.
phrases.notes: He means the workers formally agreed, with a קנין, to be responsible for the items.

phrases.english: And likewise רבי יוחנן said:
It is where they made a קנין with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, בְּשֶׁקָּנוּ מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 and resolves the challenge from steps 10, 11 and 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The weekly workers pay only because they accepted responsibility through a קנין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a special case
steps.terutzMaskana: Without a קנין, a paid guard of הקדש does not pay, just like the משנה says.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: holy items have אונאה only if one must replace them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: רבי שמעון says holy items one must replace have אונאה, and ones one need not replace do not. It then begins a ברייתא taught before רבי יצחק בר אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: holy items that a person is responsible to replace have the rules of overcharging. Those he is not responsible to replace do not. A תנא taught before רבי יצחק בר אבא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, quoting רבי שמעון's rule about אונאה. The last line is a setup: it introduces a ברייתא giving the source for רבי שמעון, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Generally holy items do not have the law of אונאה (overcharging). רבי שמעון makes an exception: if the owner must replace the animal when it is lost, it still counts as partly his own property, so אונאה applies. The ברייתא that comes next will show where he learns this.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy items, usually animals set aside for קרבנות
Responsible to replace them if lost
Overcharging or underpaying in a sale

steps.confusionAlert: Holy items are still holy items here. רבי שמעון is not saying they stop being הקדש; he is saying that when the owner must replace them, the rules of אונאה apply too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Holy items for which one is responsible to replace them –
have the rules of overcharging.
And those for which one is not responsible to replace them –
do not have the rules of overcharging.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: A תנא taught before Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: קָדָשִׁים שֶׁחַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of guarding הקדש and moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holy items the owner must replace have אונאה; holy items he need not replace do not.

steps.title: The ברייתא: holy items one must replace versus holy items one need not replace
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that for קדשים a person must replace, he is liable for a false oath, based on the words ״בה׳ וכחש״. For קדשים he need not replace, he is exempt, based on the words ״בעמיתו וכחש״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holy items that a person is responsible for: he is liable, because I read about them, "against ה׳, and deals falsely." Holy items he is not responsible for: he is exempt, because I read about them, "with his fellow, and deals falsely."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the words of the ברייתא it started to introduce in step 16. The ברייתא divides קדשים into two groups and gives each group a different law about a false oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key dividing line is אחריות, meaning whether the owner must replace the animal if it is lost. Where he must replace it, the ברייתא says he is חייב and ties this to ״בה׳ וכחש״. Where he need not replace it, he is פטור and it ties this to ״בעמיתו וכחש״. This is the same dividing line רבי שמעון used for אונאה in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy items, here sacrificial animals
Responsibility. The owner must replace the animal if it is lost
Liable. Here, he must bring an offering for his false oath
Exempt. He does not bring the offering
And he deals falsely (denies the truth)
His fellow, his neighbor

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get attached to which phrase goes with which group. In the very next step רבי יצחק says the matching looks backwards.

phrases.english: Holy items for which he bears responsibility,
he is liable, for I read regarding them:
phrases.notes: Liable here means he must bring an offering for swearing falsely.

phrases.english: "against ה׳, and deals falsely."
And those for which he does not bear responsibility,
he is exempt, for I read regarding them:
"with his fellow, and deals falsely."

steps.triggerLanguage: קָדָשִׁים שֶׁחַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן, חַיָּיב, שֶׁאֲנִי קוֹרֵא בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual text of the ברייתא that step 16 introduced as taught before רבי יצחק בר אבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קדשים one must replace, one is liable for a false oath (״בה׳ וכחש״). For קדשים one need not replace, one is exempt (״בעמיתו וכחש״).

steps.title: רבי יצחק protests that the matching is backwards
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reacts to the ברייתא with ״כלפי לייא?!״, meaning that it seems to have the two phrases attached to the wrong groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Isn't it the other way around?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק hears the ברייתא and objects right away that it looks reversed. This sets up the גמרא's next move, which will deal with his objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tied ״בה׳״ to the items the owner must replace and ״בעמיתו״ to the items he need not replace. רבי יצחק's short protest says this pairing looks flipped. He does not explain at length. The phrase itself shows he thinks the two halves should be switched.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'toward which side?' It means 'you have it backwards!'

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יצחק, answering the one who taught the ברייתא before him.

phrases.english: Isn't it the other way around?!
phrases.notes: A quick exclamation, like saying 'Which way are you facing?' He means the ברייתא has it backwards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the ברייתא just quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's matching of ״בה׳ וכחש״ and ״בעמיתו וכחש״ to the two groups of קדשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pairing of each phrase with each group appears reversed, so the ברייתא as taught seems backwards.
